elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — Customer is a Party, so a for-any-reason (convenience) right to terminate the Agreement exists (no Order Form construct in this MSA). The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false only because the right is expressed mutually as "Either Party" rather than "Customer may terminate"; in substance the Customer right is present.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Operative text requires "ninety (90) days written notice"; nothing in the redline shortens Customer's notice to 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic anywhere in 4(a); to the contrary, the retained sentence gives Kubient "all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates."

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained "Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit" plus the inserted proviso "provided Kubient may terminate only at the end of a term" means Kubient's for-any-reason exit can only take effect at a term boundary, not mid-term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 band. The one-year Initial Term lock-out is a 12-month (not multi-year) commitment, so it does not defeat the element under the detection guidance.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The only termination-related payment retained is "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" — i.e. fees actually generated during the 90-day (three-month) notice run-off, not a separate early-termination penalty. No fee formula, instalment acceleration or exit charge exceeding three months' fees survives.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Inserted proviso: "provided Kubient may terminate only at the end of a term", scoped to the for-any-reason sentence, expressly ties Kubient's convenience termination to a term boundary rather than leaving it as a bare notice right under the auto-renewal structure. Drafting nit (not a failure): "a term" is lowercase while "Term" is defined as Initial Term plus renewals; "the end of the then-current Term" would be tighter.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The mutual notice requirement "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" is retained verbatim and applies to Kubient.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: Customer keeps a 90-day for-any-reason exit after a 12-month Initial Term, no early-termination fee beyond fees generated in the 90-day run-off, and the inserted proviso confines Kubient's for-any-reason termination to a term boundary with the same 90 days' notice.

Preferred level fails on two elements: notice remains 90 days (not 30) and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund; indeed the retained sentence entitles Kubient to all fees generated during the termination period. These are correctly not pursued given the fallback is reached.

Correctly characterised as a deviation rather than natural-term non-renewal: pre-edit, the mutual for-any-reason right let Kubient exit during any renewal period with the effective date untethered from the term end, which is a Vendor mid-term convenience exit under the rule boundary.

Minimal: a single 11-word proviso appended to the existing sentence; no deletions, no survival tails, refund mechanics, expense language or procedures added, and Customer-favourable retained text (Initial Term lock-out, 4(b) breach/insolvency rights) is untouched.

Intent preserved: the proviso is scoped to the for-any-reason sentence and does not disturb 4(b) breach or immediate insolvency termination, the fee-entitlement sentence, or the auto-renewal mechanic; no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is created.

Optional tightening for the drafter (not required for completeness): change "at the end of a term" to "effective only at the end of the then-current Term" so the effective date and the defined term are unambiguous.
